Case Study 3: Southeast Asian Inti–Plasma Palm Oil · Regulation (EU) 2023/1115

Disentangling 25-Year Oil Palm Replanting from Tropical Peat-Swamp Deforestation under the EU Deforestation Regulation: Multi-Sensor Inti–Plasma Mill Supply-Shed Adjudication in Pelalawan, Riau, Indonesia

Oxeous Spatial Compliance Research Group1,*, Prepared for Department of Geoinformatics — Z_GIS2
1Oxeous Earth Observation & Automated Statutory Compliance Systems (DDS Dossier Ref: C716-ID-2026-RIAU-PALM); 2Paris Lodron University of Salzburg (PLUS), Schillerstraße 30, 5020 Salzburg, Austria. *Statutory Cutoff: 31 December 2020.

Abstract: Indonesia and Malaysia supply over 85% of European Union palm oil imports (Elaeis guineensis, CN 1511 10 90 and 1511 90 99). Under Articles 3(a) and 3(b) of the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR, Regulation (EU) 2023/1115), Southeast Asian palm oil mills sourcing Fresh Fruit Bunches (FFB) from dual Inti–Plasma (nucleus estate and smallholder cooperative) supply sheds confront two simultaneous failure modes in conventional two-dimensional (2D) satellite monitoring. First, oil palm trees reach harvest senescence at 25 years (exceeding 12–15 m trunk height) and must be rotationally felled, chipped, and replanted under Indonesia's national smallholder replanting mandate (Peremajaan Sawit Rakyat — PSR). Because mature oil palm stands exhibit closed-canopy optical reflectance (NDVI 0.81–0.83), standard 2D forest-loss products (Hansen GFC v1.13) misclassify 82% of lawful 25-year plantation replanting as illegal deforestation. Second, unsegregated mill intake allows external FFB blocks encroaching upon protected tropical peat-swamp domes (Kesatuan Hidrologis Gambut / Presidential Instruction Inpres No. 5/2019) to contaminate entire mill export consignments. This paper presents an empirical multi-sensor adjudication of a four-block Inti–Plasma supply batch (184.60 ha total across Blocks B-01 to B-04) in Pelalawan Regency, Riau Province, Sumatra (0.265°N, 102.198°E). By fusing Sentinel-2 10 m L2A optical time series, Sentinel-1 C-band SAR backscatter (Δγ0), the Nature Trace Natural Forests 2020 baseline, and the Forest Data Partnership (FDP) 10 m deep-learning oil palm probability model (palm/model_2026a) within Oxeous's PWRI-3D framework, we prove that the 16.40 ha 2022 canopy clearing in Plasma Block B-03 (44.20 ha) is lawful Article 2(5) rotational replanting on a pre-2020 oil palm plantation (ppalm = 94.6%, natural forest 1.1%). Simultaneously, Oxeous identifies and quarantines Block B-04 (41.20 ha), where 18.80 ha of primary peat-swamp forest (ppalm = 3.8%, natural peat forest 97.6%) were cleared and drained in 2022 (Δγ0 = −4.9 dB). Segregating B-04 at the mill weighbridge gate certifies the remaining 143.40 ha compliant Inti–Plasma cadastre (Blocks B-01–B-03) and its 752,400 kg Crude Palm Oil (CPO) export shipment (€790,000 value) for EU TRACES NT customs clearance.

Keywords: EU Deforestation Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2023/1115); Oil Palm (Elaeis guineensis); Article 2(5) Rotational Replanting (Peremajaan Sawit Rakyat); Tropical Peat-Swamp Forest (Inpres No. 5/2019); Forest Data Partnership 10 m Palm Model; Inti–Plasma Mill Supply Shed; Pelalawan, Riau, Indonesia.

1. Introduction: The Dual Palm Oil Compliance Crisis

Crude Palm Oil (CPO) and palm kernel derivatives (Elaeis guineensis, CN 1511 and 1513) require strict geolocation traceability down to every supplying plot of land under EUDR Article 9(1)(d). In Sumatra and Kalimantan, oil palm cultivation operates on a mandatory 25-year biological cycle. By age 25, palm trunks reach heights of 12 to 15 m, rendering manual harvesting with telescopic sickle poles hazardous and economically unviable while bunch productivity declines sharply. Under Indonesia's national smallholder replanting program (Peremajaan Sawit Rakyat — PSR, Ministry of Agriculture Regulation Permentan No. 03/2022), senescent stands are mechanically felled, trunk biomass is chipped in situ to prevent Oryctes rhinoceros beetle breeding, a leguminous cover crop (Mucuna bracteata) is established, and high-yielding Tenera seedlings are replanted along existing drainage canal grids.

From satellite orbit, a 25-year-old oil palm block exhibits dense evergreen frond closure (NDVI > 0.80) that is spectrally indistinguishable in single-date optical imagery from secondary tropical forest. When rotational felling occurs after the December 31, 2020 EUDR cutoff date, global tree-cover loss algorithms (Hansen GFC v1.13 lossyear > 20) and bitemporal optical monitors flag 100% of the felled block as catastrophic deforestation. Across Indonesia and Malaysia, more than 2.8 million hectares of aging smallholder oil palm require PSR replanting during 2021–2030; under conventional 2D GIS screening, these lawful agricultural renewals suffer an 82.0% false-rejection rate, excluding compliant smallholder cooperatives from European supply chains.

Conversely, immediately adjacent to established canal estates in Riau's Kampar–Pelalawan basin lie deep ombrotrophic tropical peat-swamp domes (Kesatuan Hidrologis Gambut — KHG). Under EUDR Article 3(b) (“produced in accordance with relevant legislation of the country of production”), clearing or excavating drainage canals into deep peat domes (>3 m peat depth) or protected peat hydrological zones violates Indonesia's Permanent Forest and Peatland Moratorium (Presidential Instruction Inpres No. 5/2019 and Government Regulation PP No. 57/2016). When a palm oil mill aggregates Fresh Fruit Bunches (FFB) from its nucleus estate (Inti) and surrounding smallholder blocks (Plasma) without pre-intake spatial verification, a single rogue supplier block encroaching into a peat-swamp dome contaminates the entire mill's CPO storage tank.

2. Study Area & Inti–Plasma Cadastre (Pelalawan, Riau)

We evaluate a four-block commercial and cooperative mill supply batch, Koperasi & PT Sawit Riau Lestari (Batch ID-RIAU-PALM-2026), located on the margin of the Kampar–Pelalawan peat dome in Riau Province, Sumatra, Indonesia (geographic centroid 0.265°N, 102.198°E; WGS84 EPSG:4326). The declared mill supply shed spans 184.60 ha divided into four canal-bounded blocks:

Nucleus Block B-01 (ID-RIA-01, 52.40 ha) and Nucleus Block B-02 (ID-RIA-02, 46.80 ha) comprise mature pre-2000 oil palm stands separated by rectilinear primary drainage canals. Plasma Cooperative Block B-03 (ID-RIA-03, 44.20 ha) is an established pre-2000 smallholder plasma block where 16.40 ha of senescent 24-year-old palms were felled and replanted in 2022 under the PSR program. South of the estate canal perimeter, third-party Block B-04 (ID-RIA-04, 41.20 ha) extends across the statutory Kampar–Pelalawan Peat-Swamp Moratorium boundary, where 18.80 ha of primary peat-swamp forest were cleared and drained in Q3 2022.

3. Methodology: Multi-Sensor Peat & PSR Engine

To disentangle lawful 25-year PSR oil palm replanting (EUDR Article 2(5) and Recital 37) from illegal tropical peat-swamp conversion (EUDR Articles 3(a) and 3(b)), Oxeous evaluates every 10 m pixel (x, y) using Rule 1: PWRI-3D Plantation vs. Peat-Forest Discrimination. Post-2020 canopy disturbance pixels (Losspost-2020 from Hansen GFC v1.13 and Sentinel-2 L2A) are intersected against the dual 2020 baseline of the Nature Trace / WRI 10 m Natural Forests 2020 probability layer (pnat,2020) and the Forest Data Partnership 10 m deep-learning oil palm probability model (ppalm,2020 from palm/model_2026a):

V3(a) = MMU≥0.5ha(Losspost-2020 ∩ {pnat ≥ 0.50}) \ {ppalm ≥ 0.65 ∧ ΔNDVI > +0.20}
(1)

A canopy disturbance cluster qualifies as exempt Article 2(5) oil palm replanting if and only if: (i) the 2020 FDP 10 m model verifies pre-cutoff oil palm occupancy (ppalm ≥ 0.65) and natural forest probability is negligible (pnat < 0.05); (ii) Sentinel-1 C-band SAR confirms the absence of new peat-drainage canal excavation (Δγ0 > −2.0 dB); and (iii) Sentinel-2 phenology tracks rapid vegetative rebound (ΔNDVI > +0.20 within 24 months) following Mucuna bracteata cover-crop establishment and young palm frond expansion. Second, at the mill supply-shed level, any supplying block Bk exhibiting V3(a)(Bk) > 0 or encroaching upon Indonesia's Protected Peat Hydrological Dome (Zpeat, Inpres No. 5/2019) is quarantined prior to FFB weighbridge intake:

P′mill = ∪ { Bk | V3(a)(Bk) = 0 ∧ A(Bk ∩ Zpeat) = 0 } = B01 ∪ B02 ∪ B03
(2)

Third, to guarantee that FFB from quarantined Block B-04 is not covertly blended into the certified mill consignment (MCPO = 752.4 t at standard Oil Extraction Rate OER = 22.0%, corresponding to 3,420 t FFB across 143.40 ha), Agent A6 enforces the regional MPOB/GAPKI Sumatra biological yield ceiling (Yc = 6.10 t CPO ha−1 yr−1):

Yimplied,CPO = MCPO / AWGS84(P′mill) = 752.4 t / 143.40 ha = 5.25 t ha−1 ≤ Yc
(3)

4. Empirical Results & Multi-Sensor Proof

As demonstrated in Figure 1 and Table 1, Oxeous resolves both compliance failures simultaneously. In Nucleus Blocks B-01 (52.40 ha) and B-02 (46.80 ha), closed-canopy oil palm fronds remained undisturbed from 2019 through 2025 (NDVI 0.82; FDP palm probability 96.8% and 96.1%). In Plasma Cooperative Block B-03 (44.20 ha), 16.40 ha of senescent 24-year-old palms were felled in Q1 2022 under the national PSR program, causing a temporary NDVI dip from 0.81 to 0.54 (Figure 2a). While 2D Hansen GFC alerts flagged B-03 as 16.40 ha of illegal deforestation, the clipped FDP 10 m probability surface (Figure 1b) proves that 94.6% of B-03 was established oil palm prior to 2020 (Nature Trace natural forest probability 1.1%). Sown leguminous cover crops and young Tenera palms restored NDVI to 0.79 by 2025-Q2, certifying B-03 under EUDR Article 2(5).

Conversely, in third-party Block B-04 (41.20 ha), the clipped FDP 10 m model reveals near-zero pre-2020 oil palm occupancy (3.8%; Figure 1b), while Nature Trace confirms 97.6% undisturbed peat-swamp forest in 2020 (Figure 2b). In Q3 2022, 18.80 ha of B-04 were cleared and drained across the Kampar–Pelalawan Peat Moratorium boundary, causing an irreversible NDVI collapse (0.86 → 0.26) and a severe Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter drop (Δγ0 = −4.9 dB from peat drainage and surface subsidence). Oxeous triggers an immediate statutory veto on B-04 under EUDR Articles 3(a) and 3(b), quarantining its FFB at the mill gate while certifying the 143.40 ha clean Inti–Plasma batch (752,400 kg CPO).

5. Discussion & Policy Conclusions

This study demonstrates that accurate EUDR enforcement in Southeast Asian palm oil requires simultaneous protection of lawful smallholder replanting (Peremajaan Sawit Rakyat) and ruthless quarantine of tropical peat-swamp destruction. By fusing the 10 m Forest Data Partnership oil palm probability baseline with Nature Trace natural forest typology and Sentinel-1 SAR drainage signatures, Oxeous eliminates the 82.0% PSR false-positive crisis on Block B-03 while preventing the 18.80 ha peatland breach in Block B-04 from entering the mill's EU export stream—certifying 752,400 kg of deforestation-free CPO (€790,000 commercial value).
